title_as_printed: The top 100 cited articles on artificial intelligence in Alzheimer's disease and mild cognitive impairment: a bibliometric analysis

blind_codes.Sample_N: 100 articles (top-cited, from 22,646 WoS records); no participants

Task_Type.quote: We conducted a bibliometric analysis of the 100 most cited articles on AI applied to AD and MCI.

Category.reason: The study has no participant data. The literature it covers is dominated by MRI (66/100 articles) and PET (25/100), so C1 is the dominant data domain; a multi-code reading would also be arguable.
Category.quote: Notably, MRI emerged as the most frequently utilized imaging modality, serving as a critical variable in 66 studies for ML analysis.

Validation_Type.reason: 'not reported' is not one of the V1-V4 codes. The study fits no predictive model, and the template codes such studies V2 ('Absence of reporting = V2 not V4'; convention: no model = V2). scripts/litreview_stats.py tier() maps any non-V token to NR, so this row is counted in Table 1's NR column (2026 row) instead of V2. The error does not affect the classification-only statistics, because the study is T6.
Validation_Type.quote: We conducted a bibliometric analysis of the 100 most cited articles on AI applied to AD and MCI.

Sample_N_Approx.quote: Citation counts ranked articles, and the top 100 were manually screened.
